variants.cost: K formation uses (t+1)k A-vector products and tk A^T-vector products; forming C uses s additional A^T-vector products. Total: (2t+1)k+s scalar matrix-vector products, s<=min(n,w). Separately charge dk Gaussian samples, dense rank-revealing orthonormalization O(n*w*min(n,w)), C^T C formation O(d*s^2), eigendecomposition O(s^3), output multiplication O(n*s*k), and completion O(n*k^2). Storage includes O(n*w+d*s+s^2+dk) numbers. Exact fallback uses at most d A-vector products, O(n*d*min(n,d)) dense SVD arithmetic and O(nd+nk) storage. For d>=2 and epsilon>=d^-2, t=O(log(d)/sqrt(epsilon)); otherwise d<1/sqrt(epsilon), apart from separately handled d=1. Overall scalar product count is O(k*log(2*d)/sqrt(epsilon)). Dense arithmetic and storage are not free; a width-k block product costs k scalar products.
variants.implementation_details_ref: PDF p.3 Algorithm 2; pp.9–10 section 5.2 and p.10 fallback discussion. Numerical constants, switching rule, actual basis dimension and completion are explicit local specifications, justified by the same-batch Theorem.
variants.name: Algorithm 2 with explicit local completion and fallback
variants.output: Z in R^{n x k}, Z^T Z=I_k. The Krylov output lies within range(K) when s>=k. When s<k, completion can add vectors outside range(K); almost surely this case has rank(A)<k and range(K)=range(A). The exact branch returns a leading singular subspace, completing zero directions when needed.
public_inputs: A in R^{n x d}; positive integers n,d; integer 1<=k<=min(n,d); epsilon in (0,1). Tuning requires only n,d,k,epsilon.
variants.query_and_update: Krylov branch: for j=1,...,t compute B_j=A(A^T B_{j-1}); retain K=[B_0,...,B_t], with w=(t+1)k columns. Let s=rank(K) and Q in R^{n x s} be an exact orthonormal basis. If s>=k, compute C=A^T Q and M=C^T C; order an orthonormal eigenbasis of M by decreasing eigenvalue and return Z=Q Ubar_k. If s<k, complete Q to k orthonormal columns by scanning e_1,...,e_n, projecting away previously selected columns, discarding zero remainders and normalizing nonzero remainders. Resolve eigenspace ties by projecting and orthonormalizing coordinate vectors within the tied eigenspace.
variants.requirements: Exact A and A^T vector products, rank-revealing orthonormalization, exact eigensolve/SVD and coordinate vectors for orthonormal completion. The exact-SVD fallback may materialize A by standard basis queries.
variants.state_and_initialization: Choose the branch from d and epsilon. In the Krylov branch draw Pi in R^{d x k} with independent N(0,1) entries and set B_0=A Pi.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: If d=1 or epsilon<d^(-2), acquire A's d columns if needed, compute its exact SVD, and return k orthonormal leading left singular vectors, completing zero singular directions by coordinate Gram-Schmidt. Otherwise set gamma=epsilon/2 and L=10^9*d*k^4. Let p be the least positive odd integer at least log2(32*d*(1+L)/epsilon)/(2*sqrt(gamma)); set t=(p-1)/2 and run exactly t block updates. The polynomial and sigma_{k+1} in the Proof are analysis objects, not tuning inputs.
